mission_2.prediction: I predict Nav2 Smac 2D will finish sooner than BFS on the constrained map.  Because BFS finds paths on a grid, which creates sharp, 90-degree corners that force the robot to constantly slow down to turn in tight spaces. Nav2 Smac 2D uses built-in smoothing to create a natural , rounded road rather than a rigid zig-zag on graph paper allowing the robot to drive through the maze faster without having to brake as often.
mission_2.performance: Nav2 Smac 2D succeeded in 73.3 s and drove 20.6 m. BFS ended as controller_failed after 99.7 s and 23.8 m. The result supported my prediction: Nav2 was faster and its path was shorter. At my checkpoint , BFS is at the bottom-right corner making a sharp 90 degree turn. The robot slows to about 0.16 m/s there and the executed line drifts about 0.1 m off the planned path. Nav2's smoothed path has rounder turns, so the robot doesn't have to slow down as much. BFS also stopped just short of the goal (0.257 m, but the limit is 0.25 m), so it was marked a failure.
mission_2.choice: I would choose Nav2 Smac 2D. It succeeded on both maps: 35.7 s on the open map and 73.3 s on the constrained map. Compared with my A*, Nav2 drove a shorter distance on both maps (10.1 m vs 13.2 m on open, 20.6 m vs 23.9 m on constrained). A* tracked the path slightly better on the open map (0.015 m vs 0.041 m tracking error), but Nav2 was faster and shorter. For delivery, getting there faster and reliably matters most to me.
